release_notes: [Important] Initial release. Valkey on Amazon Linux 2023, hardened baseline; all OS packages current at build.
short_description: Valkey (Redis-compatible) on Amazon Linux 2023, security-hardened for production: minimal package set, SSH key-only access, IMDSv2-only, bound to loopback with no default auth exposure, and continuously patched images. This product has charges associated with it for image hardening, maintenance, and support.
long_description:
Valkey (Hardened) on Amazon Linux 2023 is a production-ready, security-hardened image of the Valkey in-memory data store, maintained and supported by Derek Coleman & Associates Inc.

This is repackaged open-source software. Valkey is a Linux Foundation project - the community-driven, Redis-compatible in-memory key-value store - distributed under the BSD 3-Clause license. This product bundles unmodified upstream Valkey on a hardened Amazon Linux 2023 base; the charges associated with this listing are for image hardening, continuous patching, vulnerability scanning, and business-day support - not for the underlying open-source software, which remains free.

Hardening baseline: minimal package footprint, SSH key-only access (password authentication disabled), IMDSv2 enforced, and no exposed default authentication (Valkey binds to 127.0.0.1 until you deliberately configure bind plus requirepass or TLS in /etc/valkey/valkey.conf and open port 6379 to trusted CIDRs). Images are rebuilt, scanned for HIGH and CRITICAL vulnerabilities, and republished on a regular cadence so that new launches start current. Manage the service with systemd: sudo systemctl restart valkey.
highlights: Open-source and license-clean: Valkey is the community Redis-compatible fork; systemd-managed.
Security-hardened at build time: minimal packages, key-only SSH, IMDSv2-only, bound to loopback until you configure bind + requirepass.
Continuously patched: rebuilt, vulnerability-scanned, and republished on a regular cadence.
usage_instructions:
1. Launch from AWS Marketplace (1-Click or EC2 console).
2. Connect via SSH with your EC2 key pair: ssh -i <key> ec2-user@<public-ip>. Root login is disabled; use sudo.
3. Valkey binds to 127.0.0.1 by default. To expose it, set bind + requirepass (or TLS) in /etc/valkey/valkey.conf, then: sudo systemctl restart valkey, and open port 6379 to trusted CIDRs only.
4. Verify: sudo systemctl status valkey.
5. Sensitive data: there are no passwords or secrets anywhere in this product.
6. Backup: snapshot the EBS volume (it contains all configuration and data).
7. Resources: a single instance uses 1 EC2 instance and 1 gp3 EBS volume; no other AWS resources are created.
8. Support: support@dcassociatesgroup.com.
